sections.heading: Abstract
sections.text: OBJECTIVE. To analyze the predictive significance regarding mortality risk of clinical and laboratory parameters that can be assessed within the first 24 hours of hospitalization of sepsis patients in the intensive care unit (ICU), and to evaluate the feasibility of initiating invasive monitoring of central hemodynamics (CH) in patients with predictors of unfavorable outcome. MATERIALS AND METHODS. The results of examination of 134 patients aged 58.5 (43-71) years with abdominal sepsis were analyzed. APACHE II score was 13 (11-17) points, SOFA score was 6 (4-8) points; ICU mortality was 47%. CH was studied using transpulmonary thermodilution. Descriptive statistics were used (data presented as median, 25th and 75th quartiles), logistic regression and ROC analysis. RESULTS. Independent predictors of fatal outcome were SOFA score > 8 points (odds ratio [OR] 1.5712; 95% confidence interval [95% CI] 1.1934-2.0686; p = 0.0001; area under the curve [AUC] 0.813; sensitivity 74%, specificity 81%) and lactate level > 1.8 mmol/l

OBJECTIVES. To analyze the predictive significance of clinical and laboratory parameters in relation to the risk of mortality, the assessment of which is available in the first 24 hours of the stay of patients with sepsis in the intensive care unit (ICU), and to assess the feasibility of starting invasive monitoring of central hemodynamics in patients with predictors of poor outcome. MATERIALS AND METHODS. We analyzed the results of examination of 134 patients aged 58.5 (43-71) years with abdominal sepsis. APACHE II score was 13 (11-17) points, SOFA score was 6 (4-8) points; ICU lethality was 47%. Central hemodynamics was studied using transpulmonary thermodilution. Descriptive statistics (data are presented as median, 25 and 75% quartiles), logistic regression and ROC analysis were used. RESULTS. Independent predictors of death were SOFA score > 8 (OR 1.5712; 95% CI 1.1934-2.0686; p = 0.0001; AUC 0.813; sensitivity 74%, specificity 81%) and lactateemia > 1.8 mmol/l (OR 3.5293; 95% CI 1.7421-7.1500; p = 0.0001; AUC 0.799; sensitivity 63%, specificity 79%). A combination of established risk factors predicted cardiac index < 2.5 l/min/m2 (OR 37.0; 95% CI 3.9167-349.5290; p = 0.002) and cardiac function index < 5.8 min-1 (OR 11.8182; 95% CI 2.8189-49.5303; p = 0.0007). CONCLUSIONS. Among clinical and laboratory parameters, the assessment of which is available in the first 24 hours of the stay of patients with sepsis in the ICU, significant predictors of fatal outcome are SOFA score > 8 points and lactateemia > 1.8 mmol/l. For the majority of patients with a combination of these risk factors, signs of myocardial dysfunction are characteristic, and for 50% there is a decrease in cardiac index to a level < 2.5 l/min/m2, which indicates the feasibility of using invasive monitoring of central hemodynamics in them, in particular using transpulmonary thermodilution.

KEY WORDS: sepsis, organ dysfunction scales, risk factors, mortality, thermodilution, hemodynamic monitoring, cardiac output

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text:
Currently, in the treatment of sepsis, it is common practice to widely use non-invasive methods of circulatory monitoring [1]. Only in the latest international recommendations for sepsis treatment has there been an indication of the need to begin invasive arterial pressure (AP) monitoring as early as possible in septic shock [2, 3]. The generally accepted algorithm remains [4], which, provided the patient is in satisfactory condition, provides for monitoring of general clinical parameters, and with deterioration of condition - echocardiographic (EchoCG) examination, while the initiation of invasive monitoring of central hemodynamics (CHD) only when EchoCG does not provide exhaustive information about cardiac function or when circulatory instability progresses and there is refractoriness to sympathomimetic drugs. It is quite logical that with such an "escalation tactic" many therapeutic measures may prove untimely. Furthermore, routine use of EchoCG as the primary measure for CHD monitoring in general-profile intensive care units (ICUs) is not always feasible and sufficiently effective [5]. At the same time, there is reason to believe that invasive CHD monitoring is indicated in patients at high risk of lethal outcome - not as a last resort, but as a standard component of intensive treatment aimed at detecting the earliest signs of myocardial dysfunction [6]. Transpulmonary thermodilution (TPTD), for example, makes it possible to identify cardiac function disorders that increase the risk of mortality and probably require targeted correction [3, 7, 8]. Thus, to objectify the indications for early initiation of invasive monitoring, in particular using TPTD, and for in-depth assessment of cardiac function, it is necessary to establish predictors of lethal outcome that are accessible for routine determination and may manifest within the first 24 hours from admission of the patient to the ICU. To test this hypothesis, a two-stage retrospective study was performed.

Objective of the study: to analyze the predictive significance regarding mortality risk of clinical and laboratory parameters, the assessment of which is available within the first 24 hours of sepsis patients' stay in the ICU, and to assess the advisability of initiating invasive CHD monitoring in patients with predictors of unfavorable outcome.

sections.heading: Materials and Methods
sections.text:
In accordance with the permission of the ethics committee of FUV GBUZ MO MONIKI named after M. F. Vladimirsky (protocol No. 11 dated 13.12.2018), a retrospective observational study was conducted on the basis of the ICU of GBUZ GKB named after V. M. Buyanov DZM and GBUZ MO MONIKI named after M. F. Vladimirsky. The retrospective study included patients with abdominal sepsis or septic shock who were in the ICU from 01.06.2019 to 01.06.2020.

Inclusion criteria for the study:
/stop age from 18 to 85 years;
/stop presence of abdominal sepsis or septic shock in accordance with "Sepsis-3" criteria [9];
/stop presence in the medical record of written informed consent of the patient for the use of invasive monitoring and treatment measures.

Exclusion criteria:
/stop death in the first hours after admission to the ICU before laboratory tests;
/stop terminal stage of oncological disease;
/stop presence according to the medical record of concomitant valvular heart disease, complicated forms of coronary heart disease and/or chronic circulatory insufficiency;
/stop pregnancy.

Criteria for exclusion:
/stop fatal outcome not related to sepsis;
/stop transfer of the patient to another department or hospital.

A total of 267 medical records were selected, complete compliance with inclusion criteria was established in 157 patients. Reasons for non-inclusion in the study: death in the first hours after admission to the ICU before laboratory tests (n = 13), terminal stage of oncological disease (n = 55), presence of concomitant valvular heart disease and complicated forms of coronary heart disease, chronic circulatory insufficiency (n = 40), pregnancy (n = 2). 23 patients were excluded from the study; reasons for exclusion: fatal outcome not related to sepsis (n = 17), transfer to another department or hospital (n = 6).

Data from 134 patients (men, n = 82; women, n = 52) aged 22-85 (58.5 [43-71]) years with abdominal sepsis complicating acute destructive pancreatitis (n = 45), acute gangrenous appendicitis (n = 7), perforated duodenal or gastric ulcer (n = 26), intestinal perforation (n = 25), intestinal obstruction (n = 8), acute destructive cholecystitis (n = 4), acute cholangitis (n = 7), obstructive pyelonephritis (n = 4), ulcerative colitis (n = 1), mesenteric thrombosis (n = 4), bladder perforation (n = 1), ovarian rupture (n = 1), stab wound of the colon and small intestine (n = 1) were analyzed. The severity of condition upon admission to the ICU according to the APACHE II scale was 4-31 (13 [11-17]) points, according to the SOFA scale - 1-14 (6 [4-8]) points. Sympathomimetic drugs in the first 24 hours of ICU stay were prescribed in 86 (64%) observations; septic shock was diagnosed in 26.9% of cases (n = 36); ICU mortality was 47% (n = 63).

All patients received initial antibiotic therapy with a broad-spectrum drug with anti-anaerobic effect, or a combination, one component of which had anti-anaerobic effect. In 25% of observations, meropenem (3 g/day) was prescribed, in 25% imipenem-cilastatin (3 g/day), in 50% - a combination of ceftriaxone (4 g/day) and metronidazole (1.5 g/day). Based on the results of bacteriological cultures, initial therapy was continued or cefoperazone-sulbactam, cefepime, or a combination of ciprofloxacin and amikacin was started.

Infusions of balanced crystalloid solutions, prescription of sympathomimetic drugs and other therapeutic measures were performed in accordance with "Sepsis-3" recommendations [9]. The decision to prescribe norepinephrine (NE) was made within the first hour after the patient's admission to the ICU if, as a result of infusion, mean arterial pressure (MAP) did not reach 65 mm Hg. In the first 24 hours from admission, all patients underwent central venous catheterization (subclavian and/or internal jugular).

At the first stage of the study, in all 134 observations, demographic indicators were analyzed, assessment of the severity of patients' condition upon admission to the ICU according to APACHE II and SOFA scales, MAP, heart rate (HR), laboratory indicators (lactate level, pH of central venous blood), determined by standard laboratory methods in the first day of intensive treatment after initial stabilization of the patient's condition as a result of recommended intensive care measures [9]. In addition, information about the content in venous blood plasma of N-terminal fragment of B-type natriuretic peptide precursor (NT-proBNP) and procalcitonin (PCT) was analyzed, if these data were obtained in the first 24 hours of patients' ICU stay. NT-proBNP was determined by photometric method using an automatic analyzer Dimension Xpand Plus (Siemens, USA); PCT - by immunoassay method using a miniVIDAS analyzer (BioMerieux, France). The inotropic index (II) and vasoactive-inotropic index (VII) were retrospectively calculated in conventional units (c.u.) [10]:
/stop II (c.u.) = dopamine dose (mcg/kg/min) + dobutamine dose (mcg/kg/min) + epinephrine dose (mcg/kg/min) × 100;
/stop VII (c.u.) = NE dose (mcg/kg/min) × 100 + dopamine dose (mcg/kg/min) + dobutamine dose (mcg/kg/min) + epinephrine dose (mcg/kg/min) × 100.

At the second stage of the study, patients were selected in whom invasive monitoring of central hemodynamics using transpulmonary thermodilution (TPTD) was established in the interval 24-72 hours from admission to the ICU according to general clinical indications by standard methodology [11]. This sample included 52 patients (men, n = 33; women, n = 19) aged 22-83 (48 [39-64]) years. Sympathomimetic drugs were prescribed in 63.4% of observations (n = 33); ICU mortality was 30.7% (n = 16). At the time of TPTD initiation, all patients were on mechanical ventilation and received sedation with propofol.

During retrospective analysis, patients were divided into 2 subgroups: with the presence of a combination of mortality risk factors (n = 14) and without risk factors (n = 38). As risk factors, predictors of fatal outcome established at the first stage of the study were considered (SOFA > 8 points and lactate level > 1.8 mmol/l).

Cardiac index (CI), indexed systemic vascular resistance (ISVR), stroke volume index (SVI), global end-diastolic volume index (GEDVI), as well as global ejection fraction (GEF) and cardiac function index (CFI = GEDVI/CI, normal - 4.5-6.5 min-1) were recorded. The cardiac power index (CPI = CI × MAP / 451) and the indicator "cardiac performance determined by afterload" (CPDA) were retrospectively calculated [6]:

Statistical analysis was performed using Microsoft Office Excel and MedCalc 15 software packages. The nature of data distribution was determined using the Kolmogorov-Smirnov and Shapiro-Wilk tests. Data were presented as maximum (max) and minimum (min) values, median (Me), 25th and 75th quartiles (P25-P75), and with normal distribution - additionally as mean values (M) and standard errors (m). Differences in unrelated samples with distribution other than normal were determined using the Mann-Whitney test, with normal distribution using Student's t-test. Differences in feature frequencies (P) were assessed using Fisher's exact test.

The effect of independent variables on the dependent variable, coded binarily, was assessed using logistic regression. Odds ratio (OR), 95% confidence interval (95% CI) and significance of effect (p) were calculated. To assess the discriminatory ability of independent variables (differentiation of patients with and without the feature), ROC analysis was performed. Only those indicators that demonstrated predictive significance according to logistic regression data were included. Areas under ROC curves (AUC), 95% CI AUC and statistical significance (p) were analyzed. Model quality was considered excellent at AUC > 0.9, very good at 0.8-0.89, good at 0.7-0.79, fair at 0.6-0.69, unsatisfactory at 0.5-0.59. The threshold value (TV) of the variable was determined by the Youden index (requirement for maximum sum of sensitivity and specificity), the requirement for test sensitivity approaching 80%, and the requirement for balance between sensitivity and specificity (minimum difference between these values). The TV was taken as the value that best corresponded to all three requirements.

At the first stage of the study, fatal outcome (1 - died, 0 - survived) was used as the dependent variable, and age, sex, APACHE II and SOFA scores, MAP, HR, lactate level, pH, II and VII were used as independent variables. At the second stage of the study, CI value (1 - CI < 2.5 l/min/m2, 0 - CI > 2.5 l/min/m2) and CFI (1 - CFI < 5.8 min-1, 0 - CFI > 5.8 min-1) [7] were used as dependent variables, and the presence of a combination of risk factors, also coded binarily (1 - combination of risk factors present, 0 - combination of risk factors absent), was used as the independent variable.

Differences and identified relationships were considered significant at p < 0.05.

sections.heading: Results of the study
sections.text:
Upon admission to the ICU, assessment using the APACHE II and SOFA scales indicated the presence of sepsis and demonstrated severe condition in the majority of patients. The median value of mean arterial pressure (Table 1) corresponded to the recommended level for patients with sepsis. In 7% of patients, mean arterial pressure was below 70 mm Hg, and in 14.9% it was above 100 mm Hg. The median heart rate indicated moderate tachycardia. Heart rate greater than 90 min-1 was recorded in 76% of patients. Norepinephrine was prescribed to 61.2% of patients, additional sympathomimetic agents to 26.1% of patients, and the values of systemic vascular resistance index and cardiac index varied. Hyperlactatemia (> 2 mmol/l) was detected in 37.3% of observations. The values of mixed venous oxygen saturation and pH fluctuated within wide ranges, exceeding the boundaries of physiological norm. However, the mean values of the indicators corresponded to the latter. The presence of bacterial infection was confirmed by procalcitonin level > 0.05 ng/ml in 92.5% of patients, with biomarker values exceeding 0.5 ng/ml in 76% of observations. Values of NT-proBNP exceeding the upper limit of normal (450 pg/ml) were detected in 87% of patients, and in many observations this excess was multiple-fold.

Table 1. Clinical and laboratory data in patients (n = 134) with abdominal sepsis on admission to the ICU

Among the indicators whose registration was possible in the early period after patient admission to the ICU (Table 2), prognostic significance was demonstrated by APACHE II and SOFA scores, as well as lactatemia. The remaining parameters were not associated with mortality.

Multiple regression analysis including three independent predictors confirmed the significance of the SOFA score (OR 1.4179; 95% CI 1.0374-1.9380; p = 0.029) and lactatemia (OR 2.7536; 95% CI 1.2859-5.8965; p = 0.009). The APACHE II score lost its predictive significance (OR 1.006; 95% CI 0.8177-1.2390; p = 0.951).

In ROC analysis, the SOFA score provided a model of very good quality (AUC 0.813; 95% CI 0.698-0.897; p < 0.0001); a cutoff value > 8 points demonstrated sensitivity of 74% and specificity of 81%. The lactatemia model also approached the level of very good quality: AUC 0.799 (95% CI 0.684-0.887; p < 0.0001); a cutoff value > 1.8 mmol/l provided sensitivity of 63% and specificity of 79%. In combined ROC analysis of both predictors (Fig. 1), the AUC increased to 0.847 (95% CI 0.738-0.923; p < 0.0001), indicating improvement in the discriminatory ability of the model.

At the initiation of invasive hemodynamic monitoring (2nd stage of the study), a combination of risk factors for fatal outcome was detected in 26.9% of observations. In subgroups of patients with or without risk factors, standard hemodynamic parameters and the intensity of sympathomimetic therapy did not differ (Table 3). However, a number of hemodynamic parameters that integrally characterize cardiac pump function (cardiac index, cardiac contractility index, left ventricular stroke work index, cardiac function index, global fluid responsiveness index) were significantly lower in patients with a combination of risk factors. In the 1st subgroup, the frequency of cardiac index reduction to a level below 2.5 l/min/m2 was 50%, and in the 2nd subgroup it was 2.7% (p = 0.0002). The frequency of cardiac function index reduction to a level below 5.8 min-1 was 78.6% and 26.3% (p = 0.00002), respectively.

The combination of risk factors for fatal outcome established in the study was an independent predictor of cardiac index < 2.5 l/min/m2 (OR 37.0; 95% CI 3.9167-349.5290; p = 0.002) and cardiac function index values < 5.8 min-1 (OR 11.8182; 95% CI 2.8189-49.5303; p = 0.0007).

sections.heading: Discussion
sections.text:
Mortality from sepsis remains high even in the most developed countries in the world [12], which maintains constant interest in improving intensive care measures in this clinical situation [2]. An important component of the latter is circulatory monitoring, however, its optimal variant has not been definitively established. The attitude toward invasive monitoring of central hemodynamics remains extremely reserved, and it is recommended only in the most severely ill patients [4]. There remains an uncertain approach to maintaining cardiac pump function: on the one hand, it is not recommended to deliberately correct cardiac index [13], on the other hand, it is indicated that inotropic drugs are indicated for myocardial dysfunction [2], the methodology for detecting which also remains a subject of discussion. In particular, it is recommended to consider as the main indication for prescribing drugs that improve myocardial inotropism persistent hypoperfusion despite infusions and vasopressor administration [2].

In the latest consensus documents on sepsis treatment [2, 14], echocardiography is recommended for assessing cardiac function, without detailing its protocol. At the same time, early stages of septic myocardial dysfunction, and especially disturbances in relaxation processes, can be detected only with sufficiently complex echocardiographic techniques requiring expert-level equipment and high researcher qualification [15, 16]. In the practice of general-profile domestic intensive care units, standard bedside echocardiography with assessment of cardiac pump function by left ventricular ejection fraction and its volumes is most often available. This examination does not provide reliable diagnosis of septic cardiomyopathy and does not discriminate patients at high risk of mortality [5, 17]. As a result, timely detection of cardiac dysfunction becomes difficult, and the prescription of adequate corrective measures, in particular inotropic drugs, may be delayed, not significantly improving the condition of patients with pronounced signs of persistent hypoperfusion. We venture to suggest that the most recent data on higher mortality in sepsis patients receiving dobutamine and epinephrine [18] are explained not so much by iatrogenic effects of these sympathomimetics as by the absence of verified indications for their timely administration.

We believe that the task of early diagnosis of cardiac pump dysfunction and establishing indications for beginning inotropic therapy can be solved with invasive monitoring of central hemodynamics, in particular transpulmonary thermodilution, which is quite easily implemented in general-profile intensive care units [11]. Previously conducted studies have shown that a number of parameters determined by transpulmonary thermodilution possess predictive significance regarding mortality risk [5, 8, 19]. One such indicator is the cardiac function index, which reflects the ratio of cardiac output to preload [11]. A certain level of cardiac function index, persisting despite standard intensive care (fluid loading, vasopressors), indicates the presence of myocardial dysfunction [3, 7]. There is reason to consider cardiac function index as a possible target indicator when prescribing inotropic drugs.

Obviously, the earliest possible initiation of invasive central hemodynamic monitoring cannot be recommended for all sepsis patients, but it may be well justified in patients at risk of fatal outcome, the high probability of which is established in the first day of intensive care. Therefore, the first stage of the study was devoted to identifying early predictors of fatal outcome. Having analyzed the prognostic significance regarding mortality risk of general clinical and laboratory indicators whose registration is possible within the first 24 hours of the patient's stay in the intensive care unit, we established that the fatal outcome can be predicted most confidently in patients with a combination of a sufficiently high SOFA score and a tendency toward hyperlactatemia. All other indicators, including procalcitonin level and the myocardial stress biomarker NT-proBNP [20], did not provide early identification of patients at risk of mortality.

Both identified risk factors are standard components of clinical and laboratory examination of sepsis patients. The SOFA score, proposed more than 25 years ago [21], retains undoubted relevance in assessing mortality risk [22, 23]. Moreover, evidence has now been obtained of the association of components of this scale with disturbances in intracellular signaling pathways in sepsis, changes in matrix and mitochondrial RNA levels [24]. It is indicated that the cardiac subscale of SOFA in the first 24 hours of intensive care unit stay can stratify mortality risk in sepsis patients with concomitant cardiovascular disease, as well as in the combination of septic and cardiogenic shock [25]. The positive predictive value and negative predictive value of SOFA score established in the present work, indicating high risk of fatal outcome, practically coincided with the results of the most recent studies devoted to the predictive ability of this scale [26].

Hyperlactatemia is a recognized indicator of tissue hypoxia resulting from hypoperfusion characteristic of sepsis [27]. The established negative predictive value turned out to be somewhat lower than the level of hyperlactatemia characteristic of septic shock [9]. We believe this is quite natural, since increased mortality risk can occur in patients without clear manifestations of septic shock in the first day of intensive care unit stay [27, 28]. It is fundamentally important that the predictive ability regarding mortality in the analyzed clinical observations became more pronounced when the established SOFA score and a certain level of lactatemia were combined. We believe that it is precisely in such clinical observations that indications arise for early initiation of transpulmonary thermodilution, as there is good reason to assume the presence of myocardial dysfunction contributing to the worsening of tissue hypoxia [29].

The second stage of the study was devoted to testing the hypothesis about indications for invasive central hemodynamic monitoring in patients at high mortality risk. The obtained results confirmed the assumption about the need for early comprehensive assessment of circulatory system status in patients with established predictors of fatal outcome. In this group of observations, mean arterial pressure, heart rate, and intensity of sympathomimetic therapy were the same as in other patients. However, practically all central hemodynamic parameters reflecting cardiac pump function and myocardial contractility (cardiac index, cardiac contractility index, right ventricular stroke work index, cardiac function index, global end-diastolic volume index) [11] were reduced.

At the same time, global end-diastolic volume index and systemic vascular resistance index, changes in which are considered typical for distributive septic shock [8], did not differ. Depression of cardiac pump function in the absence of differences in preload and afterload provides grounds to consider the main cause of myocardial contractility disturbance to be the complex of pathological processes characteristic of septic cardiomyopathy [30, 31]. Depression of contractility, in turn, objectively confirms the need for inotropic drug prescription [2].

It should be noted that significant reduction in cardiac index, providing grounds to suggest a combination of sepsis with cardiogenic shock [29] and registered in half of observations with the combination of established mortality risk factors, was diagnosed, though not maximally frequently, but 18.5 times more often than in patients without such a combination. We believe this is a sufficiently strong argument in favor of early initiation of invasive central hemodynamic monitoring for timely detection of cardiac pump dysfunction not yet leading to extremely pronounced clinical presentation, in particular to persistent peripheral hypoperfusion.

At the same time, detailed analysis of the predictive significance of various transpulmonary thermodilution parameters [7] showed that the discriminatory ability of cardiac index, right ventricular stroke work index, and global end-diastolic volume index regarding high mortality risk against the background of corrective measures conducted in the first several days of the patient's intensive care unit stay may significantly worsen. Moreover, myocardial contractility disturbance may persist in patients with normal cardiac index [6]. The aforementioned cardiac function index indicates the persistence of myocardial dysfunction persisting during the first several days of the patient's intensive care unit stay despite standard corrective measures, while the negative predictive value of cardiac function index < 5.8 min-1 is associated with mortality [7]. The combination of risk factors proved to be a significant predictor of cardiac function index < 5.8 min-1, which was detected in the majority of patients in the corresponding subgroup.

It should be noted that cardiac index determination is feasible using various methods, including noninvasive ones, however, assessment of cardiac function index is possible only with transpulmonary thermodilution. Invasive central hemodynamic monitoring in such a clinical situation becomes not a last resort to understand the causes of the patient's progressive critical condition, but an important diagnostic tool allowing detection of signs of myocardial dysfunction not yet manifesting clinically but requiring certain corrective measures.

While acknowledging a certain controversial nature of the proposal to initiate invasive central hemodynamic monitoring as early as possible in patients at high mortality risk, we note that in recent years there has been a clear increase in interest in septic cardiomyopathy and its pathogenetic role in sepsis outcomes [30, 31]. There is a notable increase in interest in cardiac function and the correctness of circulatory assessment in the latest clinical recommendations [2], in particular, one can note emphasis on inotropic effects and indication of the advisability of invasive blood pressure monitoring in the development of septic shock. It can be assumed that sufficiently widespread but justified use of transpulmonary thermodilution, which has no higher risk of complications than standard invasive blood pressure monitoring, will have a positive effect on the quality of intensive sepsis treatment. As indications for early initiation of transpulmonary thermodilution, one can consider the combination of SOFA score > 8 points and lactatemia > 1.8 mmol/l.

We believe that this study has limitations: retrospective nature, limited number of clinical observations, and inability to include expert-level echocardiographic data in the analysis.

OBJECTIVES. To analyze the predictive significance of clinical and laboratory parameters in relation to the risk of mortality, the assessment of which is available in the first 24 hours of the stay of patients with sepsis in the intensive care unit (ICU), and to assess the feasibility of starting invasive monitoring of central hemodynamics in patients with predictors of poor outcome. MATERIALS AND METHODS. We analyzed the results of examination of 134 patients aged 58.5 (43-71) years with abdominal sepsis. APACHE II score was 13 (11-17) points, SOFA score was 6 (4-8) points; ICU lethality was 47%. Central hemodynamics was studied using transpulmonary thermodilution. Descriptive statistics (data are presented as median, 25 and 75% quartiles), logistic regression and ROC analysis were used. RESULTS. Independent predictors of death were SOFA score > 8 (OR 1.5712; 95% CI 1.1934-2.0686; p = 0.0001; AUC 0.813; sensitivity 74%, specificity 81%) and lactateemia > 1.8 mmol/l (OR 3.5293; 95% CI 1.7421-7.1500; p = 0.0001; AUC 0.799; sensitivity 63%, specificity 79%). A combination of established risk factors predicted cardiac index < 2.5 l/min/m2 (OR 37.0; 95% CI 3.9167-349.5290; p = 0.002) and cardiac function index < 5.8 min-1 (OR 11.8182; 95% CI 2.8189-49.5303; p = 0.0007). CONCLUSIONS. Among clinical and laboratory parameters, the assessment of which is available in the first 24 hours of the stay of patients with sepsis in the ICU, significant predictors of fatal outcome are SOFA score > 8 points and lactateemia > 1.8 mmol/l. For the majority of patients with a combination of these risk factors, signs of myocardial dysfunction are characteristic, and for 50% there is a decrease in cardiac index to a level < 2.5 l/min/m2, which indicates the feasibility of using invasive monitoring of central hemodynamics in them, in particular using transpulmonary thermodilution.

Introduction
Currently, in the treatment of sepsis, it is common practice to widely use non-invasive methods of circulatory monitoring [1]. Only in the latest international recommendations for sepsis treatment has there been an indication of the need to begin invasive arterial pressure (AP) monitoring as early as possible in septic shock [2, 3]. The generally accepted algorithm remains [4], which, provided the patient is in satisfactory condition, provides for monitoring of general clinical parameters, and with deterioration of condition - echocardiographic (EchoCG) examination, while the initiation of invasive monitoring of central hemodynamics (CHD) only when EchoCG does not provide exhaustive information about cardiac function or when circulatory instability progresses and there is refractoriness to sympathomimetic drugs. It is quite logical that with such an "escalation tactic" many therapeutic measures may prove untimely. Furthermore, routine use of EchoCG as the primary measure for CHD monitoring in general-profile intensive care units (ICUs) is not always feasible and sufficiently effective [5]. At the same time, there is reason to believe that invasive CHD monitoring is indicated in patients at high risk of lethal outcome - not as a last resort, but as a standard component of intensive treatment aimed at detecting the earliest signs of myocardial dysfunction [6]. Transpulmonary thermodilution (TPTD), for example, makes it possible to identify cardiac function disorders that increase the risk of mortality and probably require targeted correction [3, 7, 8]. Thus, to objectify the indications for early initiation of invasive monitoring, in particular using TPTD, and for in-depth assessment of cardiac function, it is necessary to establish predictors of lethal outcome that are accessible for routine determination and may manifest within the first 24 hours from admission of the patient to the ICU. To test this hypothesis, a two-stage retrospective study was performed.

Objective of the study: to analyze the predictive significance regarding mortality risk of clinical and laboratory parameters, the assessment of which is available within the first 24 hours of sepsis patients' stay in the ICU, and to assess the advisability of initiating invasive CHD monitoring in patients with predictors of unfavorable outcome.

Materials and Methods
In accordance with the permission of the ethics committee of FUV GBUZ MO MONIKI named after M. F. Vladimirsky (protocol No. 11 dated 13.12.2018), a retrospective observational study was conducted on the basis of the ICU of GBUZ GKB named after V. M. Buyanov DZM and GBUZ MO MONIKI named after M. F. Vladimirsky. The retrospective study included patients with abdominal sepsis or septic shock who were in the ICU from 01.06.2019 to 01.06.2020.

Inclusion criteria for the study:
/stop age from 18 to 85 years;
/stop presence of abdominal sepsis or septic shock in accordance with "Sepsis-3" criteria [9];
/stop presence in the medical record of written informed consent of the patient for the use of invasive monitoring and treatment measures.

Exclusion criteria:
/stop death in the first hours after admission to the ICU before laboratory tests;
/stop terminal stage of oncological disease;
/stop presence according to the medical record of concomitant valvular heart disease, complicated forms of coronary heart disease and/or chronic circulatory insufficiency;
/stop pregnancy.

Criteria for exclusion:
/stop fatal outcome not related to sepsis;
/stop transfer of the patient to another department or hospital.

A total of 267 medical records were selected, complete compliance with inclusion criteria was established in 157 patients. Reasons for non-inclusion in the study: death in the first hours after admission to the ICU before laboratory tests (n = 13), terminal stage of oncological disease (n = 55), presence of concomitant valvular heart disease and complicated forms of coronary heart disease, chronic circulatory insufficiency (n = 40), pregnancy (n = 2). 23 patients were excluded from the study; reasons for exclusion: fatal outcome not related to sepsis (n = 17), transfer to another department or hospital (n = 6).

Data from 134 patients (men, n = 82; women, n = 52) aged 22-85 (58.5 [43-71]) years with abdominal sepsis complicating acute destructive pancreatitis (n = 45), acute gangrenous appendicitis (n = 7), perforated duodenal or gastric ulcer (n = 26), intestinal perforation (n = 25), intestinal obstruction (n = 8), acute destructive cholecystitis (n = 4), acute cholangitis (n = 7), obstructive pyelonephritis (n = 4), ulcerative colitis (n = 1), mesenteric thrombosis (n = 4), bladder perforation (n = 1), ovarian rupture (n = 1), stab wound of the colon and small intestine (n = 1) were analyzed. The severity of condition upon admission to the ICU according to the APACHE II scale was 4-31 (13 [11-17]) points, according to the SOFA scale - 1-14 (6 [4-8]) points. Sympathomimetic drugs in the first 24 hours of ICU stay were prescribed in 86 (64%) observations; septic shock was diagnosed in 26.9% of cases (n = 36); ICU mortality was 47% (n = 63).

All patients received initial antibiotic therapy with a broad-spectrum drug with anti-anaerobic effect, or a combination, one component of which had anti-anaerobic effect. In 25% of observations, meropenem (3 g/day) was prescribed, in 25% imipenem-cilastatin (3 g/day), in 50% - a combination of ceftriaxone (4 g/day) and metronidazole (1.5 g/day). Based on the results of bacteriological cultures, initial therapy was continued or cefoperazone-sulbactam, cefepime, or a combination of ciprofloxacin and amikacin was started.

Infusions of balanced crystalloid solutions, prescription of sympathomimetic drugs and other therapeutic measures were performed in accordance with "Sepsis-3" recommendations [9]. The decision to prescribe norepinephrine (NE) was made within the first hour after the patient's admission to the ICU if, as a result of infusion, mean arterial pressure (MAP) did not reach 65 mm Hg. In the first 24 hours from admission, all patients underwent central venous catheterization (subclavian and/or internal jugular).

At the first stage of the study, in all 134 observations, demographic indicators were analyzed, assessment of the severity of patients' condition upon admission to the ICU according to APACHE II and SOFA scales, MAP, heart rate (HR), laboratory indicators (lactate level, pH of central venous blood), determined by standard laboratory methods in the first day of intensive treatment after initial stabilization of the patient's condition as a result of recommended intensive care measures [9]. In addition, information about the content in venous blood plasma of N-terminal fragment of B-type natriuretic peptide precursor (NT-proBNP) and procalcitonin (PCT) was analyzed, if these data were obtained in the first 24 hours of patients' ICU stay. NT-proBNP was determined by photometric method using an automatic analyzer Dimension Xpand Plus (Siemens, USA); PCT - by immunoassay method using a miniVIDAS analyzer (BioMerieux, France). The inotropic index (II) and vasoactive-inotropic index (VII) were retrospectively calculated in conventional units (c.u.) [10]:
/stop II (c.u.) = dopamine dose (mcg/kg/min) + dobutamine dose (mcg/kg/min) + epinephrine dose (mcg/kg/min) × 100;
/stop VII (c.u.) = NE dose (mcg/kg/min) × 100 + dopamine dose (mcg/kg/min) + dobutamine dose (mcg/kg/min) + epinephrine dose (mcg/kg/min) × 100.

At the second stage of the study, patients were selected in whom invasive monitoring of central hemodynamics using transpulmonary thermodilution (TPTD) was established in the interval 24-72 hours from admission to the ICU according to general clinical indications by standard methodology [11]. This sample included 52 patients (men, n = 33; women, n = 19) aged 22-83 (48 [39-64]) years. Sympathomimetic drugs were prescribed in 63.4% of observations (n = 33); ICU mortality was 30.7% (n = 16). At the time of TPTD initiation, all patients were on mechanical ventilation and received sedation with propofol.

During retrospective analysis, patients were divided into 2 subgroups: with the presence of a combination of mortality risk factors (n = 14) and without risk factors (n = 38). As risk factors, predictors of fatal outcome established at the first stage of the study were considered (SOFA > 8 points and lactate level > 1.8 mmol/l).

Cardiac index (CI), indexed systemic vascular resistance (ISVR), stroke volume index (SVI), global end-diastolic volume index (GEDVI), as well as global ejection fraction (GEF) and cardiac function index (CFI = GEDVI/CI, normal - 4.5-6.5 min-1) were recorded. The cardiac power index (CPI = CI × MAP / 451) and the indicator "cardiac performance determined by afterload" (CPDA) were retrospectively calculated [6]:

Statistical analysis was performed using Microsoft Office Excel and MedCalc 15 software packages. The nature of data distribution was determined using the Kolmogorov-Smirnov and Shapiro-Wilk tests. Data were presented as maximum (max) and minimum (min) values, median (Me), 25th and 75th quartiles (P25-P75), and with normal distribution - additionally as mean values (M) and standard errors (m). Differences in unrelated samples with distribution other than normal were determined using the Mann-Whitney test, with normal distribution using Student's t-test. Differences in feature frequencies (P) were assessed using Fisher's exact test.

The effect of independent variables on the dependent variable, coded binarily, was assessed using logistic regression. Odds ratio (OR), 95% confidence interval (95% CI) and significance of effect (p) were calculated. To assess the discriminatory ability of independent variables (differentiation of patients with and without the feature), ROC analysis was performed. Only those indicators that demonstrated predictive significance according to logistic regression data were included. Areas under ROC curves (AUC), 95% CI AUC and statistical significance (p) were analyzed. Model quality was considered excellent at AUC > 0.9, very good at 0.8-0.89, good at 0.7-0.79, fair at 0.6-0.69, unsatisfactory at 0.5-0.59. The threshold value (TV) of the variable was determined by the Youden index (requirement for maximum sum of sensitivity and specificity), the requirement for test sensitivity approaching 80%, and the requirement for balance between sensitivity and specificity (minimum difference between these values). The TV was taken as the value that best corresponded to all three requirements.

At the first stage of the study, fatal outcome (1 - died, 0 - survived) was used as the dependent variable, and age, sex, APACHE II and SOFA scores, MAP, HR, lactate level, pH, II and VII were used as independent variables. At the second stage of the study, CI value (1 - CI < 2.5 l/min/m2, 0 - CI > 2.5 l/min/m2) and CFI (1 - CFI < 5.8 min-1, 0 - CFI > 5.8 min-1) [7] were used as dependent variables, and the presence of a combination of risk factors, also coded binarily (1 - combination of risk factors present, 0 - combination of risk factors absent), was used as the independent variable.

Differences and identified relationships were considered significant at p < 0.05.
Results of the study
Upon admission to the ICU, assessment using the APACHE II and SOFA scales indicated the presence of sepsis and demonstrated severe condition in the majority of patients. The median value of mean arterial pressure (Table 1) corresponded to the recommended level for patients with sepsis. In 7% of patients, mean arterial pressure was below 70 mm Hg, and in 14.9% it was above 100 mm Hg. The median heart rate indicated moderate tachycardia. Heart rate greater than 90 min-1 was recorded in 76% of patients. Norepinephrine was prescribed to 61.2% of patients, additional sympathomimetic agents to 26.1% of patients, and the values of systemic vascular resistance index and cardiac index varied. Hyperlactatemia (> 2 mmol/l) was detected in 37.3% of observations. The values of mixed venous oxygen saturation and pH fluctuated within wide ranges, exceeding the boundaries of physiological norm. However, the mean values of the indicators corresponded to the latter. The presence of bacterial infection was confirmed by procalcitonin level > 0.05 ng/ml in 92.5% of patients, with biomarker values exceeding 0.5 ng/ml in 76% of observations. Values of NT-proBNP exceeding the upper limit of normal (450 pg/ml) were detected in 87% of patients, and in many observations this excess was multiple-fold.

Table 1. Clinical and laboratory data in patients (n = 134) with abdominal sepsis on admission to the ICU

Among the indicators whose registration was possible in the early period after patient admission to the ICU (Table 2), prognostic significance was demonstrated by APACHE II and SOFA scores, as well as lactatemia. The remaining parameters were not associated with mortality.

Multiple regression analysis including three independent predictors confirmed the significance of the SOFA score (OR 1.4179; 95% CI 1.0374-1.9380; p = 0.029) and lactatemia (OR 2.7536; 95% CI 1.2859-5.8965; p = 0.009). The APACHE II score lost its predictive significance (OR 1.006; 95% CI 0.8177-1.2390; p = 0.951).

In ROC analysis, the SOFA score provided a model of very good quality (AUC 0.813; 95% CI 0.698-0.897; p < 0.0001); a cutoff value > 8 points demonstrated sensitivity of 74% and specificity of 81%. The lactatemia model also approached the level of very good quality: AUC 0.799 (95% CI 0.684-0.887; p < 0.0001); a cutoff value > 1.8 mmol/l provided sensitivity of 63% and specificity of 79%. In combined ROC analysis of both predictors (Fig. 1), the AUC increased to 0.847 (95% CI 0.738-0.923; p < 0.0001), indicating improvement in the discriminatory ability of the model.

At the initiation of invasive hemodynamic monitoring (2nd stage of the study), a combination of risk factors for fatal outcome was detected in 26.9% of observations. In subgroups of patients with or without risk factors, standard hemodynamic parameters and the intensity of sympathomimetic therapy did not differ (Table 3). However, a number of hemodynamic parameters that integrally characterize cardiac pump function (cardiac index, cardiac contractility index, left ventricular stroke work index, cardiac function index, global fluid responsiveness index) were significantly lower in patients with a combination of risk factors. In the 1st subgroup, the frequency of cardiac index reduction to a level below 2.5 l/min/m2 was 50%, and in the 2nd subgroup it was 2.7% (p = 0.0002). The frequency of cardiac function index reduction to a level below 5.8 min-1 was 78.6% and 26.3% (p = 0.00002), respectively.

Table 2. Predictive significance of clinical and laboratory data recorded in the first 24 hours in the ICU for mortality

Table 3. Hemodynamic parameters at the beginning of invasive monitoring (n = 52)

Fig. 1. ROC-curves reflecting the discriminatory ability of lactatemia and disease severity according to the SOFA scale in relation to mortality

The combination of risk factors for fatal outcome established in the study was an independent predictor of cardiac index < 2.5 l/min/m2 (OR 37.0; 95% CI 3.9167-349.5290; p = 0.002) and cardiac function index values < 5.8 min-1 (OR 11.8182; 95% CI 2.8189-49.5303; p = 0.0007).
Discussion
Mortality from sepsis remains high even in the most developed countries in the world [12], which maintains constant interest in improving intensive care measures in this clinical situation [2]. An important component of the latter is circulatory monitoring, however, its optimal variant has not been definitively established. The attitude toward invasive monitoring of central hemodynamics remains extremely reserved, and it is recommended only in the most severely ill patients [4]. There remains an uncertain approach to maintaining cardiac pump function: on the one hand, it is not recommended to deliberately correct cardiac index [13], on the other hand, it is indicated that inotropic drugs are indicated for myocardial dysfunction [2], the methodology for detecting which also remains a subject of discussion. In particular, it is recommended to consider as the main indication for prescribing drugs that improve myocardial inotropism persistent hypoperfusion despite infusions and vasopressor administration [2].

In the latest consensus documents on sepsis treatment [2, 14], echocardiography is recommended for assessing cardiac function, without detailing its protocol. At the same time, early stages of septic myocardial dysfunction, and especially disturbances in relaxation processes, can be detected only with sufficiently complex echocardiographic techniques requiring expert-level equipment and high researcher qualification [15, 16]. In the practice of general-profile domestic intensive care units, standard bedside echocardiography with assessment of cardiac pump function by left ventricular ejection fraction and its volumes is most often available. This examination does not provide reliable diagnosis of septic cardiomyopathy and does not discriminate patients at high risk of mortality [5, 17]. As a result, timely detection of cardiac dysfunction becomes difficult, and the prescription of adequate corrective measures, in particular inotropic drugs, may be delayed, not significantly improving the condition of patients with pronounced signs of persistent hypoperfusion. We venture to suggest that the most recent data on higher mortality in sepsis patients receiving dobutamine and epinephrine [18] are explained not so much by iatrogenic effects of these sympathomimetics as by the absence of verified indications for their timely administration.

We believe that the task of early diagnosis of cardiac pump dysfunction and establishing indications for beginning inotropic therapy can be solved with invasive monitoring of central hemodynamics, in particular transpulmonary thermodilution, which is quite easily implemented in general-profile intensive care units [11]. Previously conducted studies have shown that a number of parameters determined by transpulmonary thermodilution possess predictive significance regarding mortality risk [5, 8, 19]. One such indicator is the cardiac function index, which reflects the ratio of cardiac output to preload [11]. A certain level of cardiac function index, persisting despite standard intensive care (fluid loading, vasopressors), indicates the presence of myocardial dysfunction [3, 7]. There is reason to consider cardiac function index as a possible target indicator when prescribing inotropic drugs.

Obviously, the earliest possible initiation of invasive central hemodynamic monitoring cannot be recommended for all sepsis patients, but it may be well justified in patients at risk of fatal outcome, the high probability of which is established in the first day of intensive care. Therefore, the first stage of the study was devoted to identifying early predictors of fatal outcome. Having analyzed the prognostic significance regarding mortality risk of general clinical and laboratory indicators whose registration is possible within the first 24 hours of the patient's stay in the intensive care unit, we established that the fatal outcome can be predicted most confidently in patients with a combination of a sufficiently high SOFA score and a tendency toward hyperlactatemia. All other indicators, including procalcitonin level and the myocardial stress biomarker NT-proBNP [20], did not provide early identification of patients at risk of mortality.

Both identified risk factors are standard components of clinical and laboratory examination of sepsis patients. The SOFA score, proposed more than 25 years ago [21], retains undoubted relevance in assessing mortality risk [22, 23]. Moreover, evidence has now been obtained of the association of components of this scale with disturbances in intracellular signaling pathways in sepsis, changes in matrix and mitochondrial RNA levels [24]. It is indicated that the cardiac subscale of SOFA in the first 24 hours of intensive care unit stay can stratify mortality risk in sepsis patients with concomitant cardiovascular disease, as well as in the combination of septic and cardiogenic shock [25]. The positive predictive value and negative predictive value of SOFA score established in the present work, indicating high risk of fatal outcome, practically coincided with the results of the most recent studies devoted to the predictive ability of this scale [26].

Hyperlactatemia is a recognized indicator of tissue hypoxia resulting from hypoperfusion characteristic of sepsis [27]. The established negative predictive value turned out to be somewhat lower than the level of hyperlactatemia characteristic of septic shock [9]. We believe this is quite natural, since increased mortality risk can occur in patients without clear manifestations of septic shock in the first day of intensive care unit stay [27, 28]. It is fundamentally important that the predictive ability regarding mortality in the analyzed clinical observations became more pronounced when the established SOFA score and a certain level of lactatemia were combined. We believe that it is precisely in such clinical observations that indications arise for early initiation of transpulmonary thermodilution, as there is good reason to assume the presence of myocardial dysfunction contributing to the worsening of tissue hypoxia [29].

The second stage of the study was devoted to testing the hypothesis about indications for invasive central hemodynamic monitoring in patients at high mortality risk. The obtained results confirmed the assumption about the need for early comprehensive assessment of circulatory system status in patients with established predictors of fatal outcome. In this group of observations, mean arterial pressure, heart rate, and intensity of sympathomimetic therapy were the same as in other patients. However, practically all central hemodynamic parameters reflecting cardiac pump function and myocardial contractility (cardiac index, cardiac contractility index, right ventricular stroke work index, cardiac function index, global end-diastolic volume index) [11] were reduced.

At the same time, global end-diastolic volume index and systemic vascular resistance index, changes in which are considered typical for distributive septic shock [8], did not differ. Depression of cardiac pump function in the absence of differences in preload and afterload provides grounds to consider the main cause of myocardial contractility disturbance to be the complex of pathological processes characteristic of septic cardiomyopathy [30, 31]. Depression of contractility, in turn, objectively confirms the need for inotropic drug prescription [2].

It should be noted that significant reduction in cardiac index, providing grounds to suggest a combination of sepsis with cardiogenic shock [29] and registered in half of observations with the combination of established mortality risk factors, was diagnosed, though not maximally frequently, but 18.5 times more often than in patients without such a combination. We believe this is a sufficiently strong argument in favor of early initiation of invasive central hemodynamic monitoring for timely detection of cardiac pump dysfunction not yet leading to extremely pronounced clinical presentation, in particular to persistent peripheral hypoperfusion.

At the same time, detailed analysis of the predictive significance of various transpulmonary thermodilution parameters [7] showed that the discriminatory ability of cardiac index, right ventricular stroke work index, and global end-diastolic volume index regarding high mortality risk against the background of corrective measures conducted in the first several days of the patient's intensive care unit stay may significantly worsen. Moreover, myocardial contractility disturbance may persist in patients with normal cardiac index [6]. The aforementioned cardiac function index indicates the persistence of myocardial dysfunction persisting during the first several days of the patient's intensive care unit stay despite standard corrective measures, while the negative predictive value of cardiac function index < 5.8 min-1 is associated with mortality [7]. The combination of risk factors proved to be a significant predictor of cardiac function index < 5.8 min-1, which was detected in the majority of patients in the corresponding subgroup.

It should be noted that cardiac index determination is feasible using various methods, including noninvasive ones, however, assessment of cardiac function index is possible only with transpulmonary thermodilution. Invasive central hemodynamic monitoring in such a clinical situation becomes not a last resort to understand the causes of the patient's progressive critical condition, but an important diagnostic tool allowing detection of signs of myocardial dysfunction not yet manifesting clinically but requiring certain corrective measures.

While acknowledging a certain controversial nature of the proposal to initiate invasive central hemodynamic monitoring as early as possible in patients at high mortality risk, we note that in recent years there has been a clear increase in interest in septic cardiomyopathy and its pathogenetic role in sepsis outcomes [30, 31]. There is a notable increase in interest in cardiac function and the correctness of circulatory assessment in the latest clinical recommendations [2], in particular, one can note emphasis on inotropic effects and indication of the advisability of invasive blood pressure monitoring in the development of septic shock. It can be assumed that sufficiently widespread but justified use of transpulmonary thermodilution, which has no higher risk of complications than standard invasive blood pressure monitoring, will have a positive effect on the quality of intensive sepsis treatment. As indications for early initiation of transpulmonary thermodilution, one can consider the combination of SOFA score > 8 points and lactatemia > 1.8 mmol/l.

We believe that this study has limitations: retrospective nature, limited number of clinical observations, and inability to include expert-level echocardiographic data in the analysis.
Conclusion
Thus, among the clinical and laboratory indicators that can be assessed within the first 24 hours of sepsis patients' stay in the ICU, significant predictors of fatal outcome are a SOFA score > 8 points and lactate level > 1.8 mmol/l. Кроме того, рутинное использование ЭхоКГ как основной меры мониторинга ЦГД в отделениях   реанимации
и    интенсивной  терапии  (ОРИТ)  общего  профиля не  всегда  реализуемо  и  достаточно  эффективно [5]. Вместе с тем есть основания полагать, что инвазивный мониторинг ЦГД показан больным с высоким риском летального исхода -   не как крайняя мера, а как стандартный компонент интенсивного лечения, направленный на выявление самых ранних признаков миокардиальной дисфункции [6].  Транспульмональная  термодилюция (ТПТД), например, позволяет выявить нарушения функции сердца, повышающие риск летальности и, вероятно, требующие целенаправленной коррекции [3, 7, 8]. Таким образом, для объективизации показаний к раннему началу инвазивного мониторинга, в частности с помощью ТПТД, и углубленной оценки функции сердца необходимо  установление  предикторов  летального  исхода, которые  доступны  для  рутинного  определения  и  могут проявиться в течение первых суток от поступления больного в ОРИТ. Для проверки этой гипотезы выполнили   двухэтапное ретроспективное исследование.
Цель  исследования : проанализировать предикторную значимость в отношении риска летальности клинико-  лабораторных  показате  лей,  оценка  которых доступна в первые 24 ч нахождения больных с сепсисом в ОРИТ, и оценить целесообразность начала инвазивного мониторинга ЦГД у больных с предикторами неб  лагоприятного исхода.
Материалы и методы
В соответствии с разрешением этического комитета ФУВ ГБУЗ МО МОНИКИ им. М. Ф. Владимирского (протокол  № 11  от 13.12.2018)  выполнили  ретроспективное  обсервационное  исследование  на  базе  ОРИТ ГБУЗ ГКБ им. В.  М. Буянова ДЗМ и ГБУЗ МО МОНИКИ им. М.  Ф. Владимирского. В ретроспективное исследование включили больных с абдоминальным сепсисом или септическим шоком, находившихся в ОРИТ с 01.06.2019 по 01.06.2020.
Критерии включения в исследование:
/stop возраст от 18 до 85 лет;
/stop наличие абдоминального сепсиса или септического шока в соответствии с критериями «Сепсис-3» [9];
/stop наличие в медицинской карте письменного информированного согласия больного на использование инвазивных мер наблюдения и лечения. Критерии нев  ключения:
/stop смерть  в  первые  часы  после  поступления в ОРИТ до выполнения лабораторных исследований;
/stop терминальная стадия онкологического заболевания;
/stop наличие по данным медицинской карты сопутствующих клапанных заболеваний сердца, ос-
ложненных форм ишемической болезни сердца и/или хронической недо  статочности кровообращения;
/stop беременность.
Критерии исключения:
/stop летальный исход, не связанный с сепсисом;
/stop перевод больного в другое отделение или стационар.
Всего  было  отобрано  267 медицинских  карт,  полное  соответствие  критериям  включения  установлено у 157 больных. Причины нев  ключения в исследование: смерть в первые часы после поступления в ОРИТ до выполнения лабораторных исследований ( n = 13), терминальная стадия онкологического заболевания ( n = 55), наличие сопутствующих клапанных заболеваний сердца и осложненных форм ишемической болезни сердца, хронической недо  статочности кровообращения ( n = 40), беременность  ( n = 2).  Исключены  из  исследования 23 пациента,  причины  исключения:  летальный  исход, не связанный с сепсисом ( n = 17), перевод в другое отделение или стационар ( n = 6).
Проанализированы данные 134 больных (мужчины, n = 82; женщины, n = 52) в возрасте 22-85 (58,5 [43-71]) лет с абдоминальным сепсисом, осложнившим острый деструктивный панкреатит ( n = 45), острый гангренозный аппендицит ( n = 7), перфоративную язву двенадцатиперстной кишки или желудка ( n = 26), перфорацию кишечника ( n = 25), кишечную неп  роходимость ( n = 8), острый деструктивный холецистит ( n = 4), острый холангит ( n = 7), обструктивный пиелонефрит ( n = 4), язвенный колит ( n = 1), мезентериальный тромбоз ( n = 4), перфорацию мочевого пузыря ( n = 1),  разрыв  яичника  ( n = 1),  ножевое  ранение  толстой  и  тонкой  кишки ( n = 1).  Тяжесть  состояния при поступлении в ОРИТ по шкале APACHE II составила 4-31 (13 [11-17]) балл, по шкале SOFA -   1-14 (6[4-8]) баллов. Симпатомиметические препараты в первые 24 ч нахождения в ОРИТ были назначены в 86 (64 %) наблюдениях; септический шок  был  диагностирован  в  26,9 %  случаев  ( n = 36); летальность в ОРИТ составила 47 % ( n = 63).
Все больные получали стартовую антибиотикотерапию препаратом широкого спектра, имеющим антианаэробный эффект, либо комбинацию, один из компонентов которой имел антианаэробный эффект. В 25 % наблюдений назначали меропенем (3 г/сут), в 25 % имипенем-  циластатин (3 г/сут), в 50 % -   комбинацию цефтриаксона  (4 г/сут)  и  метронидазола  (1,5 г/сут). По  результатам  бактериологических  посевов  продолжали  стартовую  терапию  либо  начинали  применять цефоперазон-  сульбактам,  цефепим  или  комбинацию ципрофлоксацина и амикацина.
Инфузии сбалансированных кристаллоидных растворов, назначение симпатомиметических препаратов и  другие  лечебные  меры  выполняли  в  соответствии с рекомендациями «Сепсис-3» [9]. Решение о назначении норэпинефрина (НЭ) принимали в течение первого
часа после поступления больного в ОРИТ, если в результате инфузии среднее АД (АДср) не достигало уровня 65 мм рт. ст. В первые 24 ч от момента поступления всем больным  выполняли  катетеризацию  магистральной вены (подключичная и/или внутренняя яремная).
На первом этапе исследования во всех 134 наблюдениях  проанализированы  демографические  показатели,  оценка  тяжести  состояния  больных  при  поступлении в ОРИТ по шкалам APACHE II и SOFA, АДср, частота сердечных сокращений (ЧСС), лабораторные показатели  (лактатемия,  pH  центральной  венозной крови),  определенные  стандартными  лабораторными методами в первые сутки интенсивного лечения после первичной стабилизации состояния больного в результате  рекомендованных  мер  интенсивной  терапии [9]. Кроме  того,  анализировали  информацию  о  содержании в плазме венозной крови N-терминального отрезка предшественника натрийуретического пептида B-типа (NT-proBNP) и прокальцитонина (ПКТ), если эти данные были получены в первые 24 ч пребывания больных в ОРИТ. NT-proBNP определяли фотометрическим методом с помощью автоматического анализатора Dimension Xpand Plus (Siemens, США); ПКТ -   иммуноферментным методом с помощью анализатора miniVIDAS (BioMerieux, Франция). Ретроспективно рассчитывали инотропный индекс (ИИ) и вазоактивно-  инотропный индекс (ВИИ) в условных единицах (у. е.) [10]:
/stop ИИ (у. е.) = доза допамина (мкг/кг/мин) +   доза добутамина (мкг/кг/мин) (мкг/кг/мин) +   доза эпинефрина (мкг/кг/мин) ×   100;
/stop ВИИ (у. е.) = доза НЭ (мкг/кг/мин) ×   100 +   доза допамина (мкг/кг/мин) +   доза добутамина (мкг/ кг/мин) +   доза эпинефрина (мкг/кг/мин) ×   100.
На втором этапе исследования отобрали больных, у которых в интервале 24-72 ч от поступления в ОРИТ по общеклиническим показаниям был налажен инвазивный мониторинг ЦГД с помощью ТПТД по стандартной методике [11]. В эту выборку вошли 52 пациента (мужчины, n = 33; женщины, n = 19) в возрасте 22-83 (48 [3964]) года. Симпатомиметические препараты были назначены в 63,4 % наблюдений ( n = 33); летальность в ОРИТ составила 30,7 % ( n = 16). К моменту начала ТПТД все больные находились на ИВЛ и получали седацию пропофолом.
При ретроспективном анализе пациентов разделили на 2 подгруппы: с наличием сочетания факторов риска летальности ( n = 14) и без факторов риска ( n = 38). В качестве факторов риска рассматривали предикторы летального исхода, установленные на первом этапе исследования (SOFA > 8 баллов и лактатемия > 1,8 ммоль/л).
Регистрировали сердечный индекс (СИ), индексированные  общее  периферическое  сосудистое  сопротивление  (ИОПСС),  ударный  объем  (ИУО),  глобальный конечно-  диастолический объем (ИГКДО), а также глобальную фракцию изгнания сердца (ГФИС) и индекс функции  сердца  (ИФС = ИГКДО/СИ,  норма -   4,5-
6,5 мин -1 ). Ретроспективно рассчитали индекс мощности сердца (ИМС = СИ ×   АДср /451) и показатель «производительность сердца, обусловленная постнагрузкой» (ПСОП) [6]:
Статистический анализ выполнили с помощью программных  пакетов  Microsoft  Office  Excel  и  MedCalc  15. Характер распределения данных определяли с помощью критериев  Колмогорова-Смирнова  и  Шапиро-Уилка.  Данные  представили  в  виде  максимального  (max) и  минимального (min) значений, медианы (Me), 25-го и 75-го кварти  лей  (P25-P75),  а  при  нормальном  распределении -   дополнительно  в  виде  средних  величин  (M) и ошибок средних (m). Отличие нес  вязанных выборок при распределении,  отличном  от  нормального,  определяли с помощью критерия Манна-Уитни, при нормальном с помощью t -критерия Стьюдента. Отличия частот признаков (Р) оценивали с помощью точного критерия Фишера.
Влияние неза  висимых переменных на зависимую, закодированную бинарно, оценили с помощью логистической регрессии. Рассчитывали отношение шансов (ОШ), 95%-й доверительный интервал (95% ДИ) и значимость влияния ( р ).  Для оценки разделительной способности неза  висимых  переменных  (разграничение  больных с наличием и отсутствием признака) выполняли ROCанализ. В последний включали только те показатели, которые продемонстрировали предикторную значимость по  данным  логистической  регрессии.  Анализировали площади под ROC-кривыми (ППК), 95% ДИ ППК и статистическую значимость ( p ). Качество модели считали при ППК > 0,9 -   отличным, 0,8-0,89 -   очень хорошим, 0,7-0,79 -   хорошим, 0,6-0,69 -   средним, 0,5-0,59 -   неудовлетворительным. Пороговое значение (ПЗ) переменной определяли по индексу Юдена (требование максимальной суммы чувствительности и специфичности), требованию чувствительности теста, приближающейся к 80 %, и требованию баланса между чувствительностью и специфичностью (минимальная разность между этими значениями). За ПЗ принимали значение, в наиболь  шей степени соответствующее всем трем требованиям.
На первом этапе исследования в качестве зависимой переменной использовали летальный исход (1 умер,  0 -   выжил),  а  в  качестве  неза  висимых -   возраст, пол, оценки по шкалам APACHE II и SOFA, АДср, ЧСС, уровень лактатемии, pH, ИИ и ВИИ. На втором этапе исследования в качестве зависимых переменных использовали  значение  СИ  (1 -   СИ < 2,5 л/мин/м 2 , 0 -   СИ > 2,5 л/мин/м 2 ) и ИФС (1 -   ИФС < 5,8 мин -1 , 0 -   ИФС > 5,8 мин -1 ) [7], а в качестве неза  висимой наличие комбинации факторов риска, также закодированной бинарно (1 -   сочетание факторов риска есть, 0 -   сочетания факторов риска нет).
Отличия и выявленные зависимости считали значимыми при р < 0,05.
Результаты исследования
При  поступлении  в  ОРИТ  оценка  по  шкалам APACHE II и SOFA указывала на наличие сепсиса и свидетельствовала о тяжелом состоянии большинства больных. Медианное значение АДср (табл. 1) соответствовало рекомендуемому уровню для больных с сепсисом. У 7 % больных АДср было ниже 70 мм рт. ст., у 14,9 % выше 100 мм рт. ст. Медиана ЧСС указывала на умеренную тахикардию. ЧСС более 90 мин -1  регистрировали у 76 % больных. НЭ был назначен 61,2 % больных, дополнительные симпатомиметические средства -   26,1 %
больных, значения ВИИ и ИИ варьировали. Гиперлактатемию ( > 2 ммоль/л) выявили в 37,3 % наблюдений. Значения sVO2 и pH колебались в широких пределах, выходя  за  границы  физиологической  нормы.  Однако средние значения показате  лей соответствовали послед  ней. Наличие бактериальной инфекции подтверждалось уровнем  ПКТ > 0,05 нг/мл  у  92,5 %  больных,  причем в  76 %  наблюдений  значения  биомаркера  были  выше 0,5 нг/мл.  Значения  NT-proBNP, превышающие верхнюю границу нормы (450 пг/мл), выявили у 87 % больных,  во  многих  наблюдениях  это  превышение  было многократным.

Оценка по APACHE II предикторную значимость потеряла (ОШ 1,006; 95% ДИ 0,8177 -1,2390; р = 0,951).

Модель лактатемии также приближалась к уровню очень хорошего  качества:  ППК  0,799  (95% ДИ  0,684-0,887;
р < 0,0001);  ПЗ > 1,8 ммоль/л  обеспечивало  чувствительность 63 % и специфичность 79 %. При совместном ROC-анализе обоих предикторов (рис. 1) ППК возрастала до 0,847 (95% ДИ 0,738-0,923; р < 0,0001), что указывает на улучшение разделительной способности модели.
При начале инвазивного мониторинга ЦГД (2-й этап исследования)  сочетание  факторов  риска  летального исхода выявили в 26,9 % наблюдений. В подгруппах больных с наличием или отсутствием факторов риска стандартные показатели кровообращения и интенсивность  симпатомиметической  терапии  не  различались (табл. 3). Вместе с тем ряд параметров ЦГД, интегрально характеризующих насосную функцию сердца (СИ, ИМС, ПСОП, ИФС, ГФИС), у больных с сочетанием факторов риска были значимо ниже. Частота  снижения ИФС до уровня менее 5,8 мин -1  составила 78,6 и 26,3 % ( р = 0,00002) соответственно.
